C.41_heat_arteries_bp:
8 weeks of heat. Your arteries changed.
Sedentary adults did hot-water immersion for 8 weeks: artery function (FMD) 5.6% to 10.9%, mean blood pressure 83 to 78 mmHg (Brunt et al., 2016).
Heat as an extra tool, not a replacement for training.
Did you expect this?
#sumisura #heattherapy #bloodpressure #hearthealth #brussels
C.42_heat_38_5_core:
Hotter isn't better.
For heat adaptation, aim for a core temperature of about 38.5°C; going above it added no extra benefit (Gibson et al., 2020).
We dose heat. We don't max it.
How hot do you go?
#sumisura #saunacycling #heattraining #sauna #brussels
C.43_heat_fades_daily:
Heat adaptation fades. Fast.
Without exposure, adaptations decay by roughly 2.5% per day (Gibson et al., 2020). Frequency beats intensity; a weekly session helps you keep it.
How often do you sauna?
#sumisura #saunacycling #heattraining #consistency #brussels
C.44_heat_not_mitochondria:
What heat does NOT do.
8 weeks of local heat, 90 min a day: no change in mitochondrial content (Kim et al., 2020). For that, you train: zone 2 and intervals.
Every tool its own job.
Surprised?
#sumisura #heattherapy #mitochondria #science #brussels
C.45_heat_thigh_torque:
One thigh heated. One thigh not.
8 weeks of local heat: peak torque +7.8 Nm in the heated thigh vs +1.8 Nm in the other (Kim et al., 2020).
Heat adds a signal. To muscle, too.
Would you have guessed?
#sumisura #heattherapy #strength #sauna #brussels
C.46_heat_muscle_fibres:
Bigger muscle fibres. No training.
10 weeks of heat on the thigh: muscle fibre size +8.3% (Goto et al., 2011).
Not instead of lifting. On top of it.
Do you lift and sauna?
#sumisura #heattherapy #muscle #strength #brussels
C.47_heat_time_to_exhaustion:
3 weeks of sauna. +32% endurance.
Runners who took a sauna after training for 3 weeks: time to exhaustion +32%, about 1.9% faster in a race (Scoon et al., 2007).
Sauna after your run?
#sumisura #sauna #running #endurance #brussels
C.48_heat_sleep_safety:
Slept badly? Think twice about heat.
Short-term sleep loss impairs how your body handles heat (Keramidas & Botonis, 2021). So we check readiness before Sauna Cycling.
Bad night? Lower dose, or postpone.
Do you track your sleep?
#sumisura #saunacycling #sleep #safety #brussels
C.49_ihht_cardiac_patients:
Can't train hard? Oxygen can still be a stimulus.
In older cardiac outpatients, 5 weeks of IHHT at rest improved cardiorespiratory fitness from baseline (Glazachev et al., 2018). Specific population.
A low-strain option, not a shortcut.
#sumisura #ihht #hypoxia #hearthealth #brussels
C.50_ihht_no_multiplier:
Training + IHHT: better than training alone?
In older patients, adding IHHT to training gave no extra improvement in mobility or perceived health (Bayer et al., 2019).
We tell you who it's for, and who it isn't.
Appreciate the honesty?
#sumisura #ihht #training #science #brussels
C.51_breathing_slow_defined:
How fast do you breathe?
Normal is 10–20 breaths a minute; slow breathing is 4–10 (Russo et al., 2017). It affects your lungs, heart and nervous system.
Count yours for one minute. What did you get?
#sumisura #breathwork #breathing #nervoussystem #brussels
C.52_breathwork_stressor:
Fast breathwork isn't relaxation.
Over-breathing lowers CO2, narrows brain blood vessels and raises your stress drive (Russo et al., 2017).
It's a stressor. Program it like one.
What's your breathwork routine?
#sumisura #breathwork #stress #nervoussystem #brussels
C.53_breathhold_water_safety:
Breath holds and cold water. Never together.
Hyperventilating before a breath hold carries a real risk of blacking out.
Never in water. Never alone. Never with cold immersion.
Share this with someone who plunges.
#sumisura #coldplunge #icebath #safety #brussels
C.54_zone2_watch_wrong:
Your watch's zone 2 might be wrong.
Real zone 2 sits just below your first threshold, lactate around 1–2 mmol/L; many train at the second threshold and call it easy (Sitko et al., 2025).
Test it. Don't guess it.
What does your watch say?
#sumisura #zone2 #vo2max #endurance #brussels
C.55_zone2_not_everything:
Zone 2 isn't everything.
Zone 2 builds the base (Sitko et al., 2025); intervals and threshold work raise the ceiling.
The mix is the prescription.
How much of your training is easy?
#sumisura #zone2 #vo2max #training #brussels
C.56_vo2_vital_sign:
A stronger predictor than smoking.
The AHA calls fitness a clinical vital sign: it predicts mortality more strongly than smoking, high blood pressure, cholesterol or type 2 diabetes (Ross et al., 2016).
Do you know your VO2max?
#sumisura #vo2max #longevity #hearthealth #brussels
C.57_vo2_first_steps:
The least fit gain the most.
More than half of the drop in cardiovascular deaths comes from a very modest increase in fitness (Ross et al., 2016).
Start with volume. Then intensity.
Where are you starting from?
#sumisura #vo2max #fitness #longevity #brussels
C.58_redlight_wavelengths:
Which wavelength for what?
611–650 nm: skin. 670 nm: the morning eye studies. 810–850 nm: deeper tissue.
Wavelength, dose and timing. That's the protocol.
Did you know the numbers mattered?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #nearinfrared #photobiomodulation #brussels
C.59_shiftwave_pressure_breath_sound:
Pressure. Breath. Sound.
Shiftwave layers pressure waves with guided breathing, voice, music and soundscapes. Three inputs, one rhythm.
Health, made Sumisura.
What helps you switch off?
#sumisura #shiftwave #breathwork #nervoussystem #brussels
C.60_vo2max_bed_rest:
3 weeks in bed. 40 years of ageing.
In the Dallas Bed Rest Study, 3 weeks of bed rest at age 20 cost 26% of VO2max. 40 years of life cost 27% (McGavock et al., 2009).
Consistency is the product.
